I am a man of 38 years in Zomba, and I farm sorghum on this small plot together with some pigeon peas and cowpeas mixed in. I do not have money for fertilizer from the shop this year — the price is too high, and sorghum is strong, it can grow on our soil without it. I keep a few goats and chickens, so I will carry their manure to the field before the rains, and I will plant the seeds I saved from last harvest because they know our land. My wife and I will do most of the work ourselves; only at weeding time, when the grass is too much, I may call one or two people to help for a few days in exchange for food or a little money.
